testName: IISER IAT - Motion in a Plane (20 Questions)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The angle between vectors A = 2i + 3j and B = i - 2j is approximately:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Dot product A·B = (2)(1) + (3)(-2) = 2 - 6 = -4.
Step 2: |A| = √(4+9) = √13, |B| = √(1+4) = √5.
Step 3: cosθ = (-4)/(√13√5) = -4/√65.
Step 4: θ ≈ 119.7° ≈ 120°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two vectors P and Q have magnitudes 3 and 4. The magnitude of resultant is 5. The angle between them is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Using R² = P² + Q² + 2PQ cos θ.
Step 2: 25 = 9 + 16 + 2(3)(4) cos θ = 25 + 24 cos θ.
Step 3: 25 = 25 + 24 cos θ → cos θ = 0.
Step 4: θ = 90°. This forms a 3-4-5 right triangle.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Image-based: The figure shows vector A and vector B drawn from common point. Using parallelogram method, which diagram correctly shows the resultant A + B?
options: Diagram showing side connecting head to tail
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In parallelogram method, vectors A and B form adjacent sides.
Step 2: The resultant is the diagonal from the common tail point.
Step 3: This diagonal represents A + B using parallelogram law of vector addition.
Step 4: The other diagonal (not from common point) represents A - B.
questions.imagePrompt: Two vectors A and B drawn from common origin O at angle, completing parallelogram with opposite vertex P, diagonal OP shown as resultant R = A + B, labeled points O, A, B, P, vectors labeled with arrows, clean geometric diagram with dashed lines completing parallelogram

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A vector A of magnitude 10 makes 30° with the x-axis. The component along the y-axis is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: If a vector makes angle θ with x-axis, its y-component is A sinθ.
Step 2: A_y = 10 × sin(30°).
Step 3: sin(30°) = 1/2.
Step 4: Therefore, A_y = 10 × 1/2 = 5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The unit vector perpendicular to both A = i + j and B = j + k is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Perpendicular vector = A × B (cross product).
Step 2: A × B = |i j k|
|1 1 0|
|0 1 1| = i(1-0) - j(1-0) + k(1-0) = i - j + k.
Step 3: Magnitude = √(1+1+1) = √3.
Step 4: Unit vector = (i - j + k)/√3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A projectile is fired with velocity 50 m/s at 37° above horizontal. The horizontal range is (g = 10 m/s², sin37° = 0.6, cos37° = 0.8):
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Range R = u² sin(2θ)/g.
Step 2: sin(2×37°) = sin(74°) = 2 sin(37°) cos(37°) = 2 × 0.6 × 0.8 = 0.96.
Step 3: R = (2500 × 0.96)/10 = 2400/10 = 240 m.
Step 4: Alternatively: R = (2 × 50 × 0.6 × 50 × 0.8)/10 = (60 × 40)/10 = 240 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Image-based: The velocity-time graph shows horizontal (v_x) and vertical (v_y) components of projectile velocity. At what time is the projectile at maximum height?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: At maximum height, vertical velocity v_y = 0.
Step 2: From graph, v_y starts positive, decreases linearly, becomes zero at t₂.
Step 3: After t₂, v_y becomes negative (descending).
Step 4: Horizontal velocity v_x remains constant throughout (no air resistance).
questions.imagePrompt: Two graphs side by side: Left graph shows v_x vs t with horizontal line at constant value, right graph shows v_y vs t with straight line starting at positive value, crossing zero at t₂, continuing to negative, time axis labeled t₁, t₂, t₃, t₄, clean scientific plotting style with grid lines

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle in uniform circular motion has speed v and radius r. The angle between velocity vector and acceleration vector is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In uniform circular motion, velocity is tangent to circle.
Step 2: Acceleration (centripetal) is toward center, perpendicular to tangent.
Step 3: Therefore velocity ⊥ acceleration, angle = 90°.
Step 4: This is why speed remains constant (a ⊥ v, no component along velocity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The position vector of a particle is r = (3t²)i + (4t²)j. The trajectory is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: x = 3t², y = 4t².
Step 2: Eliminate t: y/x = 4/3 → y = (4/3)x.
Step 3: This is equation of straight line through origin with slope 4/3.
Step 4: The particle moves along this line with increasing speed (accelerated motion).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A boat crosses a river of width 100 m flowing at 2 m/s. The boat speed in still water is 4 m/s perpendicular to current. The drift downstream is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Time to cross = width / boat speed = 100/4 = 25 s.
Step 2: During this time, river carries boat downstream.
Step 3: Drift = river velocity × time = 2 × 25 = 50 m.
Step 4: Resultant velocity magnitude = √(4² + 2²) = √20 = 2√5 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Image-based: The figure shows three vectors A, B, C forming a triangle head-to-tail. Which relation is correct?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In triangle law, if vectors form closed triangle head-to-tail, their sum is zero.
Step 2: A + B + C = 0 represents closed polygon (triangle).
Step 3: This means C = -(A + B), or A + B = -C.
Step 4: The negative sign indicates opposite direction for closing the triangle.
questions.imagePrompt: Triangle with vertices P, Q, R: Vector A from P to Q, Vector B from Q to R, Vector C from R to P, forming closed triangle with arrows showing head-to-tail connection, labeled clearly, geometric diagram style

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle moves in xy-plane with position r = (2t)i + (t²)j. The acceleration vector at t = 2 s is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Velocity v = dr/dt = 2i + 2tj.
Step 2: Acceleration a = dv/dt = 0i + 2j = 2j.
Step 3: Acceleration is constant (2 m/s² in y-direction).
Step 4: At t = 2 s, a = 2j (same for all t).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The maximum height of a projectile is H. For the same initial speed, the maximum possible range is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Maximum height for a projectile is H = (u^2 sin^2θ)/(2g).
Step 2: Range is R = (u^2 sin2θ)/g.
Step 3: Maximum range occurs at θ = 45°, so R_max = u^2/g.
Step 4: If the given maximum height H corresponds to θ = 45°, then H = u^2/(4g).
Step 5: Therefore, R_max = u^2/g = 4H.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Passage: A particle moves in circular path of radius 2 m with angular velocity ω = 3t² rad/s where t is time.

Question 1: The linear speed at t = 2 s is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Angular velocity at t = 2 s: ω = 3(4) = 12 rad/s.
Step 2: Linear speed v = rω = 2 × 12 = 24 m/s.
Step 3: The motion is non-uniform circular motion (ω changes with time).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius 2 m with angular velocity ω = 3t² (rad/s). The tangential acceleration at t = 2 s is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Angular acceleration α = dω/dt = d(3t²)/dt = 6t.
Step 2: At t = 2 s, α = 6 × 2 = 12 rad/s².
Step 3: Tangential acceleration a_t = rα = 2 × 12 = 24 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Image-based: The figure shows a projectile trajectory with points P, Q, R at same height. Which statement is correct?
options: Speed at P equals speed at R
Velocity at P equals velocity at R
Time from P to Q equals time from launch to P
questions.explanation:
Step 1: For same height in projectile motion, speed is same (energy conservation).
Step 2: Velocity differs in direction (upward at P, downward at R).
Step 3: Time from P to Q equals time from Q to R (symmetry), not from launch.
Step 4: Acceleration is always g downward, never zero.
questions.imagePrompt: Parabolic trajectory with launch point O, maximum height M, landing point L, points P and R at same height on ascending and descending branches, point Q at same height between them, velocity vectors shown at P (upward angle) and R (downward angle), clean physics diagram with labeled points

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The scalar triple product A·(B × C) represents:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: B × C gives vector perpendicular to plane of B and C, magnitude = area of parallelogram.
Step 2: A·(B × C) = |A||B × C|cos φ = |A|cos φ × |B × C| = height × base area.
Step 3: This equals volume of parallelepiped formed by A, B, C.
Step 4: If zero, vectors are coplanar.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle has initial velocity u = (3i + 4j) m/s and constant acceleration a = (2i - 2j) m/s². The velocity after 2 s is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: v = u + at.
Step 2: v = (3i + 4j) + 2(2i - 2j) = (3i + 4j) + (4i - 4j).
Step 3: v = (3+4)i + (4-4)j = 7i + 0j.
Step 4: The particle moves purely in x-direction after 2 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a projectile launched at angle θ, the ratio of maximum height to range is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: H = u² sin²θ/(2g), R = u² sin(2θ)/g = 2u² sinθ cosθ/g.
Step 2: H/R = [u² sin²θ/(2g)] / [2u² sinθ cosθ/g] = sin²θ/(4 sinθ cosθ) = sinθ/(4 cosθ) = tanθ/4.
Step 3: For θ = 45°, H/R = 1/4, so H = R/4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Image-based: The figure shows vector addition using triangle method. If |A| = 3, |B| = 4, and the angle between them when placed tail-to-tail is 60°, what is |A + B|?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Using |A + B|² = |A|² + |B|² + 2|A||B|cos θ.
Step 2: |A + B|² = 9 + 16 + 2(3)(4)cos(60°) = 25 + 24 × 0.5 = 25 + 12 = 37.
Step 3: |A + B| = √37 ≈ 6.08.
Step 4: This is less than 3+4=7 (maximum when θ=0°) and more than |4-3|=1 (minimum when θ=180°).
questions.imagePrompt: Two vectors A and B with common tail O, angle 60° between them, parallelogram completed with diagonal showing A+B, magnitudes labeled |A|=3, |B|=4, angle marked as 60°, resultant vector R = A+B shown as diagonal, geometric construction with clear labels
